children: AeroVironment
shares rose 3% in extended trading Wednesday after the defense contractor
fiscal first-quarter revenue and adjusted earnings that exceeded Wall Street estimates.
Revenue rose 6% to a first-quarter record of $480.5 million from $454.7 million a year earlier. The result beat analysts’ consensus estimate of $456 million by $24.5 million, or about 5.4%.
Adjusted earnings climbed to $0.59 a share from $0.32 a year earlier. That was more than double Wall Street’s estimate of $0.25 a share.
The better-than-expected quarter may offer some relief to investors after a punishing year for the stock. As of Wednesday’s regular-session close, AeroVironment
shares were down 42% for the year.
Drone programs support demand
Investor interest in AeroVironment

centers on rising military spending for drones, loitering munitions and defenses against enemy unmanned aircraft. The Pentagon and allied governments are seeking systems that can provide surveillance or attack targets without putting pilots at risk. Recent conflicts also have demonstrated that relatively inexpensive drones can destroy equipment costing millions of dollars.
AeroVironment

makes the Switchblade family of loitering munitions, which can circle above a battlefield before striking a target. Its best-known products also include Puma reconnaissance drones, the P550 autonomous aircraft and the LOCUST laser system for disabling hostile drones.

The company recorded $683 million in quarterly bookings, producing a book-to-bill ratio of 1.4. A ratio above 1 means incoming orders exceeded recognized revenue. Funded backlog reached a record $1.5 billion, up 37% from a year earlier and 23% from the end of April.
“Our customers are continuing to field autonomous capabilities at increasing scale,” Chief Executive Wahid Nawabi said in the earnings announcement.
Autonomous systems offset weaker space, cyber sales

Revenue from the Autonomous Systems segment rose 21% to $346 million. Sales of uncrewed aircraft systems surged 71% to $120 million while revenue from precision-strike and defensive systems increased 8% to $197 million.

Those gains offset weakness in the Space, Cyber and Directed Energy segment, where revenue fell 21% to $134.5 million. Space and directed-energy sales declined 28% while cyber and mission-solutions revenue dropped 16%.
Gross margin increased to $124.6 million from $95.1 million. It widened to 26% of revenue from 21%, helped by lower amortization and other noncash expenses related to acquisition accounting.
Net income rose to a loss of $5.1 million, or $0.10 a share, from a year-earlier loss of $67.4 million, or $1.44 a share.
Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization declined to $53.4 million from $56.6 million, despite the stronger revenue and gross margin.
Full-year outlook remains unchanged
For fiscal 2027, AeroVironment
maintained its revenue forecast of $2.125 billion to $2.225 billion. The midpoint of $2.175 billion is slightly below the Wall Street consensus of $2.19 billion.
The company continues to expect adjusted earnings of $3.02 to $3.34 a share. The midpoint of $3.18 is below analysts’ consensus estimate of $3.22.
AeroVironment

also forecast net income of $10 million to $27 million, earnings of $0.21 to $0.53 a share and adjusted ebitda of $305 million to $325 million. Management expects 55% of annual revenue and about two-thirds of adjusted ebitda to arrive in the second half of the fiscal year, leaving execution weighted toward the later quarters.
